answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a meaningful stake in a shared vault before it can trade or vote. Creating thousands of fake identities then stops being cheap, because every new identity must fund its own stake and risks losing it if it misbehaves. Like a nebula slowly condensing into stars, reputation should accumulate gradually from verified work rather than appearing instantly, and like a glacier, stake should unbond slowly, so an attacker cannot spin up identities, extract value, and vanish before penalties catch up.
